cues.text: Welcome to Study Session Five of MIT 8101, Information Technology Management.
This session is titled Performance, Continuity and Resilience in IT.
Let us begin with the learning objectives for this session.
By the end of this session, you should be able to do several things.
First, you should understand performance indicators, benchmarking, the Balanced Scorecard and dashboards.
These are the tools organisations use to measure how well their information technology is performing.
Second, you should be able to distinguish efficiency from effectiveness.
These two ideas are often confused, so we will take care to separate them clearly.
Third, you should be able to explain resilience engineering and recovery models.
This is about how systems and organisations are designed to withstand disruption and to recover from it.
Fourth, you should be able to design business continuity and disaster recovery plans, so that critical services can carry on, or be restored, when something goes wrong.
Fifth, you should be able to evaluate relevant standards, so that you can judge how well a plan or practice aligns with recognised good practice.
And finally, you should be able to test and maintain recovery capabilities.
A plan that is never tested, or never kept up to date, cannot be trusted when it is needed most.
With these objectives in mind, we can move on to the content of the session.
